summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Tips Sharing: Clothing Details Edition ## Introduction Hello everyone, in this tutorial video, we will learn how to use the historical record function in Marvelous Designer. ## Navigating Previous Operations First, in Marvelous Designer, if you want to go back to the previous operation, press **Ctrl + Z** to revert to the previous action. To redo an operation, press **Ctrl + Y**. To quickly access your previous operations, click on the **Library** window and find the **History** window. In the History window, you will see the steps of previous operations. Clicking on one of the operation steps will revert your project to that specific step. The current operation steps will be displayed in orange. ## Working with Virtual Models If you are working with a virtual model that has changed its movement, note that you can only modify the movement of that model. To revert to the previous operation step, you have to click on the next step. If you have performed other operations after going back to the previous operation step, all subsequent operations will be covered. For example, after reverting to a previous operation step, you will see the operation steps that have been added subsequently. However, since we have selected a version, those operations will have been covered. ## Saving 3D Costume Records If we want to save all the virtual models and costumes in the current 3D window, we can click on the **Historical Record 3D Costume Status** located in the upper right corner of the historical record panel. When there is a 3D record in the **3D Costume Record** box in the upper left corner, it represents all objects currently in the 3D window. All objects in this window have been recorded. It is important to note that when we go back to previous operation steps, as long as we do not perform other operations, the later operation steps will not be covered. For instance, if we revert to previous operation steps and then click on the 3D costume record, we can add a new 3D costume record. However, be aware that when opening a 3D costume record, it will prompt you to delete the current work record. In other words, when you open a 3D costume record, all historical records saved prior will be deleted. ## Accessing Temporary Project Files When we double-click to open the 3D costume record, we will see that it actually opens a temporary project file. Upon opening it, you will notice that the previous operation steps have been cleared. Since we have added a 3D costume record before, we can double-click to open another costume record, following the same confirmation process. After opening, you will see that it has now switched to the costume wearing effect under the virtual model. The 3D costume records we saved are all project files stored in the **C Drive**. If you want to locate these project files, click on the file in the upper left corner to save as a project; you can find these files. After locating them, copy the path of these files and paste them where needed. Since these files are temporarily stored in the C Drive, you will need to paste them if required. ## Conclusion In essence, the 3D costume record state serves as a temporary way to save costume files. That's it for this episode introducing the 3D costume record function. See you next time. Bye bye. ```
